course.title: Camday – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 9

unit.title: Interpreting and discussing results
unit.blurb: Frequency polygons, scatter graphs and correlation, back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagrams, statistics for grouped data and choosing good representations.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Draw and interpret frequency polygons, including comparing two distributions.

O2.t: Draw and interpret scatter graphs, describe correlation and use a line of best fit.

O3.t: Use back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagrams to compare two sets of data (median and range).

O4.t: Estimate the mean, and find the modal class and the class containing the median, for grouped data.

O5.t: Choose and criticise representations of data, and draw conclusions from them.

p: A **scatter graph** plots pairs of values. **Positive correlation**: as one increases, so does the other. **Negative**: as one increases, the other decreases. **No correlation**: no pattern.
A **line of best fit** follows the trend with about as many points above as below. Use it to **estimate** values – but only inside the data range (not far outside).
A scatter graph may show that ice-cream sales and sunburn cases rise together (positive correlation). That does not mean ice cream causes sunburn: hot weather causes both.
Describe the pattern, then think about whether a third factor could explain it.
Ice-cream sales and sunburn are positively correlated, but ice cream does not cause sunburn – hot weather causes both.

p: For grouped data you do not know exact values, so use the **midpoint** of each class.
**Estimated mean = Σ(midpoint × frequency) ÷ Σ frequency.** The **modal class** has the highest frequency. The **median** is the ((n + 1)/2)th value: find which class it falls in.

lesson.q: Estimate the mean of the data in the table.

lesson.t: Why the mean from grouped data is an estimate
p: In grouped data you do not know the exact values, only the class. Using the midpoint of each class assumes the values in it average to the middle.
Estimated mean = Σ(midpoint × frequency) ÷ Σ frequency.
It is only an ESTIMATE of the mean because the exact values in each class are unknown.
